newsitem.title: DUBAI: BCCI depositors in UAE start getting repayments.
newsitem.headline: BCCI depositors in UAE start getting repayments.

text.p: Depositors in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) branches of the failed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) have begun receiving reimbursements, a local newspaper said on Friday.
Repayments to many of the UAE depositors, including those with deposits of over 20,000 dirhams ($4,450), began flowing in on Thursday, the Arabic-language al-Bayan newspaper added.
The UAE liquidation administrators said last month that UAE depositors with deposits of up to 20,000 dirhams ($5,450) on July 5, 1991 would be reimbursed fully by the UAE Central Bank in December.

After a five year struggle, a spokesman for the BCCI liquidators said in London on Monday that creditors of the bank will receive payment of $2.65 billion on Tuesday, equal to 24.5 percent of their claims. Another 10 percent of the admitted claims should be made in the next 12 to 16 months.
BCCI, founded in Luxembourg in 1972, was shut down in 1991 with debts of more than $12 billion after evidence emerged of widespread money laundering.
In the UAE, there are about 45,000 creditors, owed nearly five billion dollars.

Liquidators of the failed bank said in May that an agreement with majority shareholder, the Abu Dhabi government, was a key step towards paying the first dividend to about 250,000 creditors worldwide.
Under the agreement, Abu Dhabi, the biggest of seven emirates forming the UAE, paid $1.8 billion into a pool for distribution to creditors and depositors.
